newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama gets $91 million from international lenders.
newsitem.headline: Panama gets $91 million from international lenders.

text.p: Panama received $91 million from international lenders after undergoing economic reforms to privatize state entities, the government said Wednesday.

The funds, to be disbursed Wednesday and Thursday, include $60 million from the World Bank and the Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund of Japan, and $31 million from the International Monetary Fund, the Ministry of Planning and Economic Policy said.
The money will be used in the 1997 government budget "as one of the elements of administering public finances and preserving reasonable limits of external debt," it said in a communique.

Panama received the funds after the administration of President Ernesto Perez Balladares agreed to privatize state enterprises and monitor public finances, conditions set by the financial lenders, the statement said.
